newsitem.title: BRAZIL: A third of Brazilians do not legally "exist"-paper.
newsitem.headline: A third of Brazilians do not legally "exist"-paper.

text.p: Some 50 million Brazilians, almost a third of the population, do not have birth certificates or documents proving they legally exist, a local newspaper reported on Sunday.

Folha de S. Paulo, citing a study by the Brazilian Geography and Statistics Institute (IBGE), said 991,000 so-called "clandestines" were born in 1994, the last year studied, and many will die without ever having legally existed.

IBGE officials could not be reached Sunday to confirm the report. The newspaper quoted experts as saying the numbers without legal registry, mostly children, distort the true rate of infant mortality and other demographic statistics in Brazil.

"Part of those people will be asked to obtain documents when they go to school, serve in the army or enter the formal workforce," demographer Celso Simoes was quoted as saying. "(But) some 10 percent will do none of the above."

Jose Gregori, head of the National Human Rights Programme, was quoted as saying the high number of unregistered Brazilians reported in the study "is unacceptable in a serious country at the end of the 20th century." A person without a birth certificate, he added, "is a citizen who doesn't count, who simply doesn't exist."
Folha said the numbers of unregistered are highest in poor, rural northern and northeastern Brazil, South America's largest country with a population of about 160 million people.
In Amazonian Maranhao state, 81.96 percent of inhabitants are without legal registration of any kind while 58 of every 100 born in Pernambuco state in Brazil's northeast go unregistered, it said.
